content: Do not take amlodipine and benazepril if you are pregnant. If you become pregnant while taking this medication, contact your doctor immediately, as it may harm the fetus. The combination of amlodipine and benazepril is prescribed to treat high blood pressure. Amlodipine belongs to a class of medications called calcium channel blockers, which work by relaxing blood vessels so the heart does not have to pump as hard. Benazepril is an angiotensin-converting enzyme (ACE) inhibitor that decreases certain chemicals that tighten blood vessels, allowing blood to flow more smoothly. This medication is available as a capsule to be taken orally, usually once a day. To ensure consistency, take it at the same time every day. Follow the instructions on your prescription label carefully, and consult your doctor or pharmacist if you have any questions. Take the medication exactly as directed; do not take more or less than prescribed. Amlodipine and benazepril help control high blood pressure but do not cure it. Continue taking the medication even if you feel well, and do not stop without consulting your doctor. This medication may also be prescribed for other uses. Consult your doctor or pharmacist for more information. Before taking amlodipine and benazepril, inform your doctor and pharmacist if you are allergic to amlodipine (Norvasc), benazepril (Lotensin), or any other ACE inhibitors or medications. Provide a list of all prescription and nonprescription medications, vitamins, nutritional supplements, and herbal products you are taking, especially diuretics (water pills), lithium, or potassium supplements. Your doctor may need to adjust your doses or monitor you for side effects. Inform your doctor if you have recently experienced severe diarrhea or vomiting, or if you have a history of heart failure, lupus, scleroderma, heart disease, liver disease, kidney disease, or diabetes. Let your doctor know if you are planning to become pregnant or are breastfeeding. If you are undergoing surgery, including dental surgery, inform your doctor or dentist that you are taking this medication. Discuss with your doctor before using salt substitutes containing potassium. If your doctor prescribes a low-salt or low-sodium diet, follow these instructions carefully. If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember. However, if it is almost time for your next dose, skip the missed dose and continue your regular schedule. Do not take a double dose to make up for a missed one. Amlodipine and benazepril may cause side effects. Common side effects include cough, headache, dizziness, and swelling of the hands, feet, ankles, or lower legs. If these symptoms are severe or persistent, inform your doctor. Serious side effects are rare but require immediate medical attention. These include swelling of the face, throat, tongue, lips, or eyes; hoarseness; difficulty swallowing or breathing; fainting; severe skin rash; yellowing of the skin or eyes; or worsening chest pain. Contact your doctor immediately if you experience any of these symptoms. Report any unusual problems to your doctor. Serious side effects can also be reported to the FDA’s MedWatch Adverse Event Reporting program. Store this medication in its original container, tightly closed, and out of reach of children. Keep it at room temperature, away from excess heat and moisture (not in the bathroom). Dispose of expired or unneeded medication properly. Consult your pharmacist for disposal instructions. In case of overdose, contact your local poison control center at 1-800-222-1222. If the person has collapsed or is not breathing, call 911 immediately. Keep all appointments with your doctor and laboratory. Regular blood pressure checks are necessary to monitor your response to the medication. Your doctor may order lab tests to assess your body’s response. Do not share this medication with others. Consult your pharmacist if you have questions about refilling your prescription.
